stories.headline: One killed, two wounded in shooting near Coors Field in downtown Denver
stories.summary:
One man was killed and two others were wounded in a shooting in the 1900 block of Market Street, near Coors Field, early Saturday morning. Police received the initial report at 1:13 a.m. and transported all three victims to a hospital, where one died. The two surviving victims are in stable condition.

Investigators believe the shooting erupted after a fight between two groups escalated. No suspect information had been developed as of Saturday morning, and Denver police are asking anyone with information, photos or videos to contact Metro Denver Crime Stoppers.

The incident was the second downtown shooting within 24 hours. Two people were hospitalized after a separate shooting Friday morning near 22nd and Stout streets in the Five Points neighborhood, approximately three-quarters of a mile away. Police said the two shootings are not believed to be connected.

stories.headline: Pedestrian killed on I-25 in Weld County after walking in highway lane
stories.summary:
A pedestrian was struck and killed by a FedEx truck on southbound Interstate 25 north of Longmont early Saturday morning. The Colorado State Patrol responded at approximately 4:53 a.m. after the man was found walking northbound in the middle of the right lane of the southbound highway when the truck hit him. He died at the scene.

The Weld County coroner is expected to release the victim's identity. The 35-year-old truck driver is not expected to face charges, according to the State Patrol.

Southbound I-25 was closed between Colorado 66 and Colorado 119 northeast of Longmont for much of Saturday morning, causing significant delays. The highway reopened at approximately 10:15 a.m., according to the Colorado Department of Transportation.

stories.headline: Man dies after being struck by two vehicles while crossing Aurora road
stories.summary:
A man was killed Friday night after being hit by two vehicles while crossing South Peoria Street in Aurora. The incident occurred around 8:15 p.m. just south of East Tennessee Avenue, where the 35-year-old was crossing in the middle of the block when a southbound vehicle struck him. He was thrown into the northbound lanes, where a second vehicle hit him, and he died at the scene.

Both drivers remained at the scene and were cooperating with investigators, Aurora police said. The Arapahoe County coroner's office is responsible for identifying the victim.

The case remains under investigation. The death highlights ongoing pedestrian safety concerns along the South Peoria Street corridor in Aurora.

stories.headline: State health officials warn more than 400 Colorado stores sold contaminated marijuana vapes
stories.summary:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment issued a health safety advisory Friday warning that contaminated marijuana vaporizers were sold at more than 400 stores statewide. The vapes were produced by Denver-based manufacturer StayCon LLC and were found to contain methylene chloride, a harmful chemical, as an ingredient in the manufacturing process.

The products were sold between March 27 and September 25 at 405 stores across the state, including locations in the Denver metro area, Colorado Springs and Grand Junction. Customers are advised to check labels against the list of contaminated batches published by the state and to destroy the products or return them to the point of purchase.

Anyone who consumed the product and became ill is asked to report the experience to the Marijuana Enforcement Division. As of Friday, state officials said they had not yet received any reports of illness linked to the contaminated vapes.

stories.headline: Downtown Denver's 1800 Larimer tower adds 125,000 square feet in new and renewed leases
stories.summary:
The 1800 Larimer Street office tower in downtown Denver has secured 125,000 square feet of new and renewed tenant leases over the past year, commercial real estate firm Newmark announced this week. Tenants include law firms Morrison & Foerster and Ballard Spahr, BOOTS Construction Co., The Boettcher Foundation, First American Heritage Title Co., Kaplan Kirsch, and Newmark itself, which renewed its full-floor lease under a long-term agreement.

The 22-story, 500,000-square-foot tower is owned by an affiliate of Blackstone and operated by Beacon Capital Partners. The leasing activity follows a $13 million renovation completed in 2024 that included a new two-story lobby, upgraded amenity spaces and improvements to a 17,000-square-foot terrace.

The deals reflect a broader flight-to-quality trend in the Denver office market, where Class A buildings with modern amenities continue to attract tenants while overall downtown office availability has remained relatively stable. The tower sits near Union Station at the intersection of Denver's Central Business District and Lower Downtown, and had previously housed Xcel Energy's Colorado headquarters before the utility relocated to the T3 RiNo building in River North.

stories.headline: Denver's 56th Annual Oktoberfest draws crowds for second weekend of celebration
stories.summary:
Denver's 56th Annual Oktoberfest continued into its second weekend on Saturday, September 26, drawing participants to the traditional German festival. The event featured classic competitions including stein hoisting qualifying matches, with contestants vying for spots in the finals.

Oktoberfest is one of Denver's longest-running annual cultural festivals, celebrating German heritage with food, beer, music and competitions. The event draws thousands of attendees each year to the Larimer Street corridor in the Highlands neighborhood.

stories.headline: Broncos place rookie RB Jonah Coleman on injured reserve, sidelining him at least four games
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos placed rookie running back Jonah Coleman on injured reserve Saturday, ruling him out for a minimum of four games due to a high ankle sprain. Coleman is eligible to return as early as Week 7 when Denver travels to Arizona. The move came just days after Coleman played a key role in the Broncos' 20-13 win over Jacksonville, powering a critical late closing drive.

Head coach Sean Payton dismissed any suggestion the team was being cautious, saying flatly that if a player can play, they will play. Coleman, a fourth-round pick out of the University of Washington, had not participated in practice during the week despite being present at the facility each day.

With Coleman sidelined, Denver will rely on J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey as the top running back options against the Rams on Sunday Night Football, with Tyler Badie serving as the third back. Long snapper Mitch Fraboni was elevated from the practice squad to take Coleman's roster spot. Dobbins is also managing a hip issue suffered during the Jacksonville game.

stories.headline: Colorado Rapids president says club is stronger after record-setting transfer window despite Navarro sale
stories.summary:
The Colorado Rapids closed a busy transfer window with the signing of 17-year-old Australian prospect Akol Akon from Sydney FC on a future contract beginning July 2027. The window also featured three major attacking additions — wingers Sayed Abu Farkhi ($6 million), Morgan Whittaker ($10 million, a club record) and Ibrahim Sadiq ($1.1 million) — while striker Rafael Navarro was sold to St. Louis City for a reported MLS-record $12 million.

Rapids president Padraig Smith said the club set out with lofty ambitions and was very pleased with the results, emphasizing that the moves were intended to make the team more capable of challenging for titles. Whittaker has already scored twice in 216 minutes with the club, netting a brace in a 3-3 draw against Seattle in his first multi-goal performance.

Colorado currently sits seventh in the Western Conference with 36 points, within the nine-team playoff field with a push needed to secure a firm position. The Akon signing mirrors the club's previous development pathway for Lucas Herrington, who was later sold to Premier League side Hull City for a record $17 million.

stories.headline: Avalanche's potential Dylan Larkin pursuit would require major trade maneuvering, columnist says
stories.summary:
Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin has expanded his trade request list to include the Colorado Avalanche, according to NHL insider Elliotte Friedman on his '32 Thoughts' podcast. Larkin, 30, asked for a trade from Detroit over the summer but had initially limited his preferred destinations to three or four teams. He arrived at Red Wings training camp, which led to the team stripping him of his captaincy.

Colorado Gazette columnist Evan Rawal argues that while Larkin would be an attractive fit as a second-line center behind Nathan MacKinnon, acquiring him would require a significant trade package that general manager Joe Sakic would need to carefully construct. Larkin has exceeded 30 goals in each of the past five seasons, with 57 power-play goals over the last four years, a skill set that would complement the Avalanche's needs.

The Avalanche closed their home preseason schedule Friday with a 5-2 win over the Winnipeg Jets, with the regular season set to open September 30. Questions about Larkin's leadership and whether he is the right cultural fit for a Stanley Cup contender remain, with Rawal noting Sakic would need to conduct thorough due diligence on the off-ice dynamics before pursuing any deal.

stories.headline: Colorado ballot measures could push back against Democratic supermajority, columnist argues
stories.summary:
Colorado voters appear on track to elect Democrats to virtually every statewide office this fall while simultaneously approving ballot measures that would restrict Democratic policy priorities, according to a political column published Sunday by the Colorado Springs Gazette. Columnist Jon Caldara argues that Colorado has reinvented ticket splitting, with voters choosing Democratic candidates while using citizen initiatives to limit government reach.

Among the measures Caldara highlights are Proposition 134, which would prevent biological males from competing on girls' sports teams, and Proposition 135, which would ban gender-affirming surgeries for minors — policies that would run counter to legislation passed by the Democratic-controlled legislature. He also points to potential TABOR-related measures that could constrain tax policy.

Caldara contends the dynamic reflects voter antipathy toward the Republican brand rather than enthusiasm for Democratic governance, with suburban voters in particular using ballot measures as a check on one-party control. Colorado Democrats could potentially hold veto-proof supermajorities in both chambers of the state legislature following the November election.

stories.headline: New college admission programs at CSU Pueblo and Colorado School of Mines aim to simplify enrollment process
stories.summary:
Colorado State University Pueblo and Colorado School of Mines have launched new programs designed to make the college admissions process less burdensome for prospective students, according to CPR News. The initiatives are part of a broader effort to improve access to higher education across the state.

Details of the specific programs were not fully outlined in available reporting, but both institutions are among Colorado's prominent public universities — CSU Pueblo serving the southern Colorado region and Mines specializing in engineering, science and mathematics in Golden. Streamlining admission procedures has become a priority for Colorado higher education institutions amid concerns about enrollment trends and college affordability.
